en: The Philippines originally celebrated Independence Day on July 4 until President Diosdado Macapagal officially changed the date to June 12 in 1962.
Juan Luna won the first gold medal for his massive painting Spoliarium at the prestigious Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts in 1884.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a unique bamboo incubator to provide affordable, life-saving healthcare for premature babies in rural Philippine areas.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people, would stretch halfway around the globe if laid end to end.
The Philippine government officially declared the South Sea pearl as the national gem in 1996 to honor the country's rich marine biodiversity.
The Philippine Congress is a bicameral legislature consisting of the Senate with 24 members and the House of Representatives with over 300 members.
The pre-colonial Baybayin script was traditionally written on bamboo and leaves, and every consonant in the alphabet inherently includes an 'a' vowel sound.
The vibrant Ati-Atihan festival in Aklan originated as a historical tribute by Malay settlers to the indigenous, dark-skinned Ati people.
The core Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the literal historical practice of an entire community carrying a nipa hut to a new location.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, every citizen has the mandatory civic duty to pay taxes to fund essential government services and infrastructure.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle was officially declared the national bird in 1995 to promote the conservation of this rare, endemic species.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato weave intricate T'nalak cloth from abaca fibers using complex patterns they believe are gifted to them in dreams.
